text:
Applicant's biologists have revealed spawning runs of Lake Jocassee trout in the lower 0.8 km (0.5 miles) of Howard Creek. Sampling on five occasions in the Corbin Creek region of Howard Creek from November 1975 to February 1976 resulted in the collection of 20 rainbow trout (7 female and 13 male) and 12 brown trout (4 female and 8 male). Lengths ranged from 241 - 610 mm (9.5-24.0 in.); the weight range was 256-1,955 gm (0.6 - 4.3 lbs.). Fourteen of the 32 trout collected weighed 2.0 pounds or more (weights are reported for only 21 of the 32 trout collected). Almost all fish were ripe, and spawning was observed. Fourteen of the trout collected were marked fish stocked in Lake Jocassee in February 1974. Figures 2-12 and 2-13 show a section of Howard Creek where trout were observed and collected during the spawning run.
Applicant's personnel sampled lower Howard Creek by electroshocking in early June 1976 and found only 3 young-of-the-year trout. Similar results were obtained from sampling conducted by the South Carolina Department of Wildlife and Marine Resources. It would appear that the spawning observed in 1975-1976 was not very successful.
Portions of Howard Creek and some tributaries contain self-sustaining trout populations. Corbin Creek supports a brown trout population with 14 to 16-inch fish taken from this stream (Olmstead, 1976). Brook and brown trout have been collected in the upper reaches of Howard Creek (Garton, et al., 1976), and this stream has been described as supporting a good brook trout fishery (Geddings, 1976; Martin, 1976).
Lower Reservoir
Figure 2-14 shows the location of monitoring stations in Lake Jocassee, the existing lower reservoir for the proposed Bad Creek Project. Historical water quality data are limited due to the recent filling of the reservoir. (Reservoir sampling by Applicant was initiated in July 1973). Data have also been obtained from the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department.
Lake Jos ssee has a surface area of 7,565 acres at full pool elevation of 1,110 feet. Maximum depth near the dam is about 107 meters (350 feet) at full pool while at the outlet works for the Bad Creek Project, the maximum depth is about 60 meters (195 feet). Mean depth of the reservoir is about 47 meters (153 feet).
